endorsements.quote: (2) ensuring AI developers disclose the composition of their training data and the methodologies behind their models for full transparency
(3) requiring evaluations of how AI tools perform across different demographic groups to mitigate biases
Independent auditing bodies—sanctioned by the FDA and specialized in AI—could conduct routine, impartial evaluations of AI tools both before and after approval.
To improve oversight, post-market surveillance practices must be standardized to reduce variability in data collection and analysis, ensuring consistent monitoring of devices over time.

unlisted_practices: Mandate extensive post-market monitoring of AI medical devices and require updates to approvals if significant drift or performance degradation is detected.
Involve diverse stakeholders, including manufacturers, providers, patients, and regulators, in developing AI regulations.
Actively include patients and caregivers, especially from historically underrepresented groups, in community-sourced regulation of health AI.
Establish a specialized regulatory body with legal authority and technical expertise to oversee AI development and deployment.
Mandate registries or open-access data repositories so developers, regulators, and researchers can collaboratively monitor AI performance.
Publish public-facing summary reports from independent AI audits detailing methods, datasets, performance outcomes, and identified biases.
Offer financial incentives such as grants, tax benefits, or expedited review to companies that meet high standards for data sharing and fairness.
Invest in AI literacy for patients, advocates, and community representatives to enable meaningful participation in regulation.
Establish clinician certification programs on AI ethics, bias detection, and system evaluation, tied to continuing education or licensure renewal.
Partner with academic institutions so supervised students support real-time monitoring and evaluation of AI tools.
Prioritize patient outcomes, health system performance, and workforce impact in post-deployment evaluation of AI.
Study the impact of consumer wellness wearables and non-device clinical decision support software thoroughly.
Coordinate FDA with ONC and CMS to harmonize data standards, coverage policies, and enforcement strategies.
Fund research on regulatory frameworks for emerging AI technologies and keep guidelines for bias detection, transparency, and performance auditing rapidly updatable.
